stories.title: Trump delays new Russia sanctions law
stories.summary: On Friday night President Donald Trump issued an executive order withholding a number of sanctions that Congress had recently passed against Russia. The sanctions law, signed by Trump in September and named for the late Senator Lindsey Graham, was set to take effect on Sunday and would have allowed tariffs of up to 100 % on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, primarily China and India. The order was justified as being in U.S. national interests.
stories.why: The delay could influence global energy prices and U.S. diplomatic relations with Russia and its major oil purchasers.

stories.title: Record weekly ship attacks reported in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data shows that 12 vessels reported attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz between 5 October and 11 October, the highest weekly total since the US‑Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week recorded 10 attacks, with six vessels struck on a single Sunday and four additional attacks reported so far this week. Industry data suggests the surge has slowed the recent recovery in oil shipments through the strait.
stories.why: The rise in attacks threatens maritime safety and could disrupt global oil supplies.

stories.title: Masked Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvesters near Abu Falah in West Bank
stories.summary: Dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians during the olive harvest in farmland near Abu Falah, setting fire to cars and olive trees. A local official said 12 Palestinians were injured, including four dual Palestinian American citizens, and a foreign journalist was also hurt. One American citizen, Majdi, was struck with nail-studded sticks and needed treatment for head wounds; his elderly mother was also injured.
stories.why: The incident shows rising settler violence that endangers civilians and press freedom during routine agricultural work in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Semiconductor selloff drags US indexes lower, AI return doubts rise
stories.summary: A broad decline in semiconductor stocks pulled major US indexes down, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 1.8% and extending its longest losing streak since 2008. Investors questioned whether AI infrastructure spending will generate profitable returns despite strong chip demand. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh reiterated a neutral stance on rates at IMF talks, and cloud‑gaming firm CoreWeave dropped 9.5% amid the rout.
stories.why: The slide signals heightened risk for tech‑heavy portfolios and could pressure related equity valuations.

stories.title: Cult.fit receives SEBI observations for proposed IPO
stories.summary: Cult.fit has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on its planned IPO, which includes a fresh issue of up to Rs 950 crore and an offer for sale. The company said revenue rose 36.26% in FY26 and adjusted EBITDA margin improved as it expanded its fitness operations nationwide. It plans to use the proceeds to repay debt, open additional fitness centres and grow its sportswear business.
stories.why: The SEBI observations bring the company nearer to completing its IPO and raising capital for debt reduction and expansion.

stories.title: India’s forex reserves fall $60 billion in six weeks
stories.summary: India’s foreign exchange reserves dropped to $726.027 billion on Oct 9, down from $785.706 billion on Sep 4, a decline of about $60 billion over six weeks. The Reserve Bank of India’s market intervention to support the rupee, amid higher crude‑oil prices, rising U.S. Treasury yields and continued foreign‑investor outflows, was cited as the main cause. Foreign‑currency assets and gold reserves also fell during the period.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported that foreign exchange reserves declined by $8.578 billion to $726.027 billion in the week ended October 9, after a $12.952 billion fall the week before. Foreign‑currency assets, gold holdings, special drawing rights and the RBI’s position with the IMF all recorded declines.
